title: Hybrid quantization latency & cost estimator — working version
content:
Purpose:
This is a working spreadsheet-style estimator for mixed/hybrid quant strategies (layer-wise INT8, per-block 3-bit, and FP8 fallbacks). Intended for product and model-onboarding owners to quickly reason about 1) per-token cost, 2) mean and tail latency under batching, and 3) expected quality delta (perp / eval metric) versus baseline FP16.

High-level approach:
- Model represents inference as sequence of micro-ops across pipeline stages: token-encode, attention layers (L1..LN), MLPs, kv-cache lookup, and token-decode.
- Each layer has a quant profile: {quant-type, compute-ops, memory-bytes, dequant-overhead-ms}. We model mixed strategies by assigning a quant-type to each layer or block.
- Latency model: base per-op latency + contention from batching. Tail latency estimated using Monte Carlo on request arrival intervals and batch formation (configurable percentiles).
- Cost model: per-GPU-second * effective occupancy factor. Occupancy computed from per-request GPU time and batching efficiency. Also includes memory footprint which can change instance choice.
- Quality model: simplified delta-perp/metric per-layer quant choice calibrated from small eval grid (we store observed deltas for common architectures). Quality degradation is additive approximation with caps and interaction heuristics.

Sheets / tabs (what to expect in the exported CSV):
- Input: workload parameters (QPS, request-length-avg, P95 request length, target latency SLO, preferred instance family, batch-window-ms).
- Layer-catalog: each row = layer/block id | ops (GMAC) | params (MB) | base-latency-ms | baseline-quant=fp16 | fallback-quant=fp8 | notes. This is editable for model-specific imports.
- Quant-profiles: for each quant-type (FP16, FP8, INT8, 4-bit, 3-bit-hybrid) we list throughput multiplier vs FP16, dequant overhead, memory compression ratio, expected quality delta (empirical label).
- Strategy-grid: combinatorial sample strategies (random + heuristic sweep). Columns include assignment-string (e.g., L1-INT8,L2-3bit,L3-FP8...), est-per-token-latency-ms, est-p95-latency-ms, est-cost-per-1M-tokens, est-quality-delta, score.
- MonteCarlo: runs of N=2000 simulated requests under chosen strategy; outputs mean latency, p50/p95/p99, batch-size-dist, GPU-utilization histogram.
- Recommendations: top-5 strategies under user constraints (SLO/loss-threshold/cost-goal).
- Notes & caveats: hand-run experiments and calibration references.

Key formulas / heuristics (spreadsheet-friendly):
- per-layer-exec-time = base-latency-ms / throughput-multiplier(quant) + dequant-overhead-ms
- per-request-gpu-time = sum(per-layer-exec-time) + kv-io-ms + decode-ms
- effective-batch-efficiency = min(1, 1 - exp(-batch-window / avg-inter-arrival)) * packing-factor
  * packing-factor uses sequence-length distribution to estimate wasted tokens per batch.
- est-cost-per-1M-tokens = (per-request-gpu-time * QPS * 1M / tokens_per_request) * gpu-hour-cost / 3600
- p95-latency estimate = MonteCarlo(percentile) but quick heuristic = mean + 2 * stddev for small sanity checks.

Calibration notes (where numbers come from):
- Throughput multipliers: measured on our 80GB A100 fleet and a 24GB H100 dev node; FP8 measured with the internal kernel set (see GH PR). INT8 multipliers include kernel-level perf but exclude KV cache impact.
- Quality deltas: aggregated from 10-model sweep using eval harness; stored per-quant and per-layer-type (attn vs mlp). Use these as priors only.

Usage walkthrough (short):
1) Paste model layer list into Layer-catalog. If you have a torchscript profile payload, use the import macro (TODO: add macro in next pass).
2) Adjust workload in Input tab: set QPS, avg tokens, SLO.
3) Run Strategy-grid generator (one-button generator in sheet; or run script to produce 500 samples).
4) Inspect MonteCarlo tab for top candidates. Sort by composite score: cost * cost-weight + latency-penalty * latency-weight + quality-penalty * quality-weight.
5) Export top-2 strategies for lab test.

Example quick numbers (toy run for 1B-parameter transformer, 16 layers, avg-req=64 tokens, QPS=6):
- Baseline FP16 (no quant): per-token latency ~ 28 ms, p95 ~ 45 ms, cost per 1M tokens ~$42
- Strategy A (INT8 all layers): per-token ~ 18 ms, p95 ~ 36 ms, cost per 1M tokens ~$28, est quality delta: +0.9 perplexity (acceptable if <1.2)
- Strategy B (INT8 attn + 3-bit MLP blocks + FP8 final layer): per-token ~ 14.5 ms, p95 ~ 31 ms, cost per 1M tokens ~$22, est quality delta: +1.7 perplexity (risky for LLM-chat but ok for classifier)
- Strategy C (FP8 majority, 3-bit on cheap blocks): per-token ~ 20 ms, p95 ~ 39 ms, cost per 1M tokens ~$30, est quality delta: +0.4 (best quality preservation)

Open questions / TODOs (short checklist):
- [ ] Improve quality interaction model — current additive assumption breaks for extreme mixed strategies. Need small factorial evals (8 configs x 3 models).
- [ ] Add layer sensitivity import from eval harness (per-layer ablation metrics) so sheet can auto-suggest which layers are quant-safe.
- [ ] Expose instance selection (A100-vs-H100-vs-RTX) in cost model and memory-constraint alerts (right now only single family considered).
- [ ] Better tail-latency modeling for cold-start/kv-evictions.

Decision heuristics we currently use in the generator (stated):
- Prefer INT8 on attention if observed attn-sensitivity < 0.6 delta; prefer 3-bit or FP8 on MLPs depending on param-size/ops.
- Keep final norm/output layers at FP8 or higher unless quality loss under threshold.
- For latency-first workloads (SLO < 30ms), prefer strategies that reduce critical path ops (prune MLP, use 3-bit where compute-heavy).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally an engineer-facing sheet: expect terse cells and sticky-note style comments.
- Please add calibration runs as linked artifacts (JIRA/GH runs) with a short note in Layer-catalog when you update empirical deltas.

References and datasets used for calibration:
- internal perf runs: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/quant-2024 (table id: qrun-2024-11)
- eval harness: confluence.redwood/evals/quant-sensitivity
- kernels: PR#37 in quant-sims repo

Contact: Ava Martinez (product-optimize) — ping on #optimize-quant in Slack for immediate questions.

Rough changelog:
- 2025-02-12 create initial draft and basic estimator tabs
- 2025-02-18 added MonteCarlo tab + sample runs
- 2025-03-01 tuned multipliers after H100 microbench

Unstructured notes / scratch:
- Thinking: could add a variant that recommends per-route strategies (chat vs embeddings) and let console auto-route short queries to more quantized shards.
- Quick test idea: run ablation matrix but constrain to <=2 quant-types per strategy to reduce combinatorial explosion.

End of document.
